This is the piece of code that is trying to connect the signal that's already connected:

```cpp
if (EditorResourcePreview::get_singleton()->is_threaded()) {

			RS::get_singleton()->connect(SNAME("frame_pre_draw"), request_vp_update_once, Object::CONNECT_ONE_SHOT);

		RS::get_singleton()->request_frame_drawn_callback(callable_mp(this, &EditorResourcePreviewGenerator::DrawRequester::_post_semaphore));

		semaphore.wait();
```

It'd be easy to fix by checking if it's already connected before connecting it, but probably a better fix would be to figure out why it would be calling it twice I guess.

I get the same error message `ERROR: Signal 'frame_pre_draw' is already connected to given callable 'RS::viewport_set_update_mode' in that object.` using the following test project:

[frame-pre-draw.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20515435/frame-pre-draw.zip)

System: Godot v4.5.dev4.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 6GB (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-3570K CPU @ 3.40GHz (4 threads)

I get the error message when the main node's Font array is displayed, This is the smallest test project I managed to create. I seems that having more than one `FontVariation` resources in the exported array is required, just adding fonts to the array doesn't seem to do the trick.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16154890-b43e-42dc-9d8b-9ddbda0f8d18)

Just to add an extra bit of info, I'm getting a flood of these errors (like sometimes upwards of 40) sometimes when I open a scene, and sometimes when I save a scene. But it's not reliable. I don't know what conditions cause it to happen. I don't have to select anything.

I've also been getting these errors occasionally since 4.5. (but never before)

They are a bit random. Sometimes when the editor starts. But more often at random. Seems to be something in certain scenes that are causing it. 
Though I seem to only get it once then almost never more.
I got this on scenes without any scripts, and I've been playing around a lot with stencils, so my guess is that, it is something to do with materials.

I think I only worked on 4.5 on projects that uses stencil materials, so it might have something to do with it. 
This seems hard to pin-point, but I'll try to keep a closer eye on what I'm doing when this happens.
(it might have happened right now when I duplicated a MeshInstance3D, or a light)

For me in 4.5 I get more this errors than 4.4 . When i import glb format make it unique and change it materials to new materials never had that in 4.4 . In 4.4 was only when i put glb object in scene sometimes. It's just random...

I seem to get this error mostly so long as a surface slot, in my case I used `Surface 0` (Generally I have 2 or 3 surfaces total), is expanded and visible while I reload but it's slightly inconsistent. If 1 reload doesn't do it, usually a 2nd one does. I'm not sure if I needed to make a mesh unique to start the problem in the first place, but all my testing happened after doing that (even after reverting the mesh). I did some testing in an inherited scene from a glb file. Testing notes (4.5.1):
- All of my materials are the baked in ones from my gltf export, not unique or saved separately in my project, nor have they ever been
- The error seems to hang around, popping up in certain scenarios like project reloads or sometimes selecting any `MeshInstance3D`, but in my testing only while the inherited glb scene is open
- I don't think I can get it to happen more than once per reload
- Having a unique mesh and surface slots collapsed can also cause this issue (While no unique mesh and an expanded surface slot also can, but no unique mesh and collapsed surface slots seems to not cause any issue) but it is less consistent. Having both a unique mesh and an expanded surface slot seems more consistent
